title: Sandbox Provisioner Recipes and Tiny Integration Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact playbook for creating ephemeral developer sandboxes that mirror Redwood production inference flows for fast local validation and integration testing. Focus: tiny, reproducible setups (<= 2 containers) developers can boot in 60s, plus recommended telemetry contracts and failure-mode recipes.

Audience:
- SDK engineers integrating new runtime features
- Solutions engineers doing quick demos
- QA for smoke/regression runs on client SDKs

Assumptions:
- Developer has Docker installed and 8GB RAM free
- API keys are stored in local env (REDSDK_API_KEY) or passed to the proxy
- We accept lightweight behavioral parity (not full perf) with hosted service

Goals:
1) Minimal friction: one script to create sandbox + stubbed model backend
2) Reproducible telemetry: consistent event shape emitted to file/stdout for CI checks
3) Safety: default timeouts and circuit-breaker mocked
4) Fast onboarding: 60s happy-path to send a generation request from sample app

Quickstart (60s):
- git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter && cd sdk-starter/sandbox-recipes
- ./sandbox up --mode tiny-proxy --env-file .env.example
- export REDSDK_API_KEY=local-test-key && node examples/send-simple-prompt.js
- ./sandbox logs   # verify stub responses and telemetry lines

What ./sandbox does (tiny-proxy mode):
- Starts one tiny reverse-proxy container that accepts SDK calls on localhost:8080
- The proxy performs routing rules similar to prod: checks model-version header, enforces token limit, and forwards to an internal stub model responder implemented as a single bash/http server that returns deterministic tokens (helps deterministic tests)

Sample SDK init snippet (JS):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ baseUrl: 'http://localhost:8080', apiKey: process.env.REDSDK_API_KEY, timeoutMs: 4500 });
const out = await client.generate({ model: 'tiny-stub-v1', prompt: 'Summarize: ...' });
console.log(out.text);

Telemetry contract (line-delimited JSON to stdout or file):
- event: string ("request.start"|"request.end"|"cache.hit"|"cache.miss"|"error.circuit")
- request_id: string (uuid)
- model: string
- sequence_len: integer
- tokens_out: integer
- latency_ms: integer
- outcome: string ("success"|"fallback"|"error")
Example line:
{"event":"request.end","request_id":"8f6b...","model":"tiny-stub-v1","sequence_len":128,"tokens_out":42,"latency_ms":82,"outcome":"success"}

Acceptance checks for a PR using the sandbox:
- ./sandbox up runs without error locally
- SDK sample can complete a generation end-to-end against the proxy
- Telemetry file contains a request.start and request.end for the run with matching request_id
- If implementing new header behavior, the proxy rejects missing header with 401 and emits error.circuit

Common failure modes and recipes:
1) "Proxy 502 / backend down": Ensure stub responder container is healthy (./sandbox ps). If flapping, increase stub start delay to allow container to warm.
2) "Timeouts in CI": Lower concurrency in sandbox by setting SANDBOX_CONCURRENCY=1 and increase client timeout. CI runners may be CPU-constrained.
3) "Mismatched telemetry schema": Run telemetry-lint (scripts/telemetry-lint) to check required fields; failing fields generate a small diff JSON to help devs fix shape quickly.

Rollout gating for changes to SDK proto/headers:
- Add a sandbox test harness case under /tests/sandbox that runs the new header flows against the tiny-proxy and fails the build if any request ends with outcome!=success.
- Add a Linear task linking to the RFC and attach sample stdout lines from the sandbox run.

Developer checklist before merge:
- [ ] Local ./sandbox up succeeds on mac/linux with default env file
- [ ] Example apps updated and passing against tiny-proxy
- [ ] Telemetry-lint passes and a small sample telemetry dump committed to the PR (for reviewers)
- [ ] README quickstart updated (1-paragraph)

Notes / open questions:
- Do we want the sandbox to optionally mimic Dedicated routing (quota enforcement) or keep only minimal logic for onboarding? Decision: MVP keeps minimal routing; expand later if teams request real quota behavior.
- Consider adding a small jitted quantized stub to better stress test tokenizer behavior without requiring GPUs.

Next steps (owner: Aisha):
- Iterate on scripts to make up/down idempotent and to support ephemeral named sandboxes (./sandbox up --name alice-test)
- Add a small GH Action that runs sandbox smoke tests on PRs that touch SDK surface
- Schedule a 30-minute sync with Solutions Eng (Priya) to demo the happy-path and gather friction notes

Appendix: Useful commands
- ./sandbox up --mode tiny-proxy --detach
- ./sandbox down --name alice-test
- ./sandbox logs --follow
- ./sandbox exec proxy -- cat /var/log/redwood/telemetry.log | jq .

End of playbook (working draft). Comments welcome — add inline or ping in #dev-experience.
